scenario.summary: A multi-stage ClickFix campaign uses sponsored Google search results for 'Amazon Business' to lead victims to fake login pages and CAPTCHAs that trigger pastejacked commands. These commands abuse the 'finger' utility to download a convoluted sequence of loaders, including IronPython and Node.js, which ultimately deliver Doina malware and Lumma Stealer via process hollowing.

meta.rationale: Focus on workstations and endpoints where end users would likely be browsing. Exclude developer machines where Node.js or Python might legitimately run from unusual paths.
meta.hypothesis: An adversary is deploying portable Node.js and IronPython interpreters to user-writable directories to execute obfuscated Doina loaders and Lumma infostealers.

hunt.name: Amazon ClickFix Multi-stage Malware Infection
hunt.description: This hunt targets the subsequent stages of the Amazon-themed ClickFix campaign. It identifies portable runtimes (IronPython and Node.js) operating from unusual paths like ProgramData or Temp, uses prevalence analysis to distinguish them from standard software, and corroborates the activity using HTTP telemetry for barbeque-themed C2 domains and specific payload URIs. The campaign culminate in the execution of the Doina loader and fileless Lumma Stealer which profiles the host and beacons via websockets.

config.scoping_notes: Focus on workstations and endpoints where end users would likely be browsing. Exclude developer machines where Node.js or Python might legitimately run from unusual paths.
config.beyond_detection: This is a hunt because a simple rule for Node.js execution is too noisy. We use fleet-wide stack counting for process paths and join with specific HTTP URI patterns to build a high confidence picture of a multi-stage infection.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, process_path, process_cmd_line, user_name, on_disk, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE instr(',' || '{{interpreter_names}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(process_name) || ',') > 0 AND (LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%\\programdata\\%' OR LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%\\users\\public\\%' OR LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%\\temp\\%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Identify Node.js or IronPython interpreters in user-writable directories to find campaign staging.
config.expected_signal: Execution of node.exe or ipyw32.exe from paths like C:\ProgramData\NodeView. Processes with on_disk = 0 suggest successful memory injection.

config.content: SELECT LOWER(process_path) AS path, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS hosts, COUNT(*) AS runs, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_process_activity WHERE instr(',' || '{{interpreter_names}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(process_name) || ',') > 0 AND (LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%\\programdata\\%' OR LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%\\users\\public\\%' OR LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%\\temp\\%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY LOWER(process_path) HAVING hosts <= 3 ORDER BY hosts, runs
config.description: Stack count the specific interpreter paths to isolate malicious deployments from standard developer workstations.
config.expected_signal: Interpreter paths appearing on only a few hosts, indicating likely malware staging directories like NodeView.
